roadmapTask: Redesign the FeatureSync dashboard UI (packages/dashboard): replace the one long scrolling environment page with a persistent left side menu navigating Segments / Versions / Flags, use the wasted horizontal space at the sides, move new/edit actions into modal dialogs instead of inline forms, and put every delete/detach action behind a confirmation dialog. A fifth operator request — accumulate edits as a pending draft and publish to S3 only on an explicit Update, with a review-pending-changes dialog — is deferred to the next horizon.

dimensions.evidence: All three destructive actions route through renderConfirmation and name their subject: delete names the flag, detach names the segment keys, the flag and the rule number, remove-rollout names the percentage, the rule label and the flag. The confirm control is the real submit carrying name=field with value delete/detachSegment/removeRollout; the trigger is an inert type=button with no name=field. grep -rn danger-zone packages/dashboard/src returns only two negative assertions - the disclosure and the comment calling it the confirmation step are both gone. Above a 9: the last single-click destructive POST path was removed structurally, the Remove submit lifted out of the shared rollout form so confirming cannot also save rollout fields (pinned by a no-name=percentage assertion), and the Playwright spec proves against real S3 state that closing the dialog leaves the attachment intact.

dialogId escapes every non [A-Za-z0-9-] char to _XXXX and joins with _, itself escaped inside parts, so the mapping is injective; modal-dialog.test.ts pins the dotted/slashed key, the separator-collision case and case preservation. Ids are scoped by flag key AND rule index, asserted per rule in rollout-form.test.ts, and two flags get two different delete ids. The scheme takes no URL-state input and flag-page.test.ts shows the single-flag page renders the identical id. Not a 10: the passCriteria bullet asking for a programmatic document.querySelectorAll('[id]') duplicate scan over a rendered multi-flag page has no equivalent in the suite, and the grader could not run a browser.

The phase's file list and diff touch only views files plus the two deleted .danger-zone CSS rules; no http-server.ts, application or domain file is in it, and http-server.test.ts is not part of this phase's diff. Every confirmation form is built from the existing WriteFormContext, so the base-version hidden input and URL state survive the move; confirm-dialog.test.ts asserts the exact action + baseVersion + state prefix and rollout-form.test.ts asserts baseVersion and ruleIndex inside both the detach and remove confirm forms. Not a 10: the two curl bullets (no/wrong Origin rejection, stale expected-current-version conflict byte-identical) were not executed - verified by diff scope and preserved form fields only.

Un-enhanced, .modal-dialog is display:block/position:static so all three confirmations are ordinary inline cards, the trigger carries hidden and is only unhidden by app.js after is-enhanced, and no confirmation passes openOnLoad - so with JS off the confirm submit is one click away and nothing is stranded. The Cancel failureExample is structurally impossible: Close is a separate form method=dialog in .dialog-head, hidden while not enhanced, never inside the destructive form. The 100% branch coverage gate is green and the tests assert subjects rather than mere existence. segment-picker.spec.ts is updated in this diff (click Detach, assert the named dialog, verify Close does NOT detach by re-reading the S3 snapshot, then confirm) and flag-page.test.ts is updated and green; the unlisted sibling spec segment-upload-rollout.spec.ts still passes in the 16/16 run. Re-scored 10 -> 9 by the orchestrator: this dimension's own 10-bar is 'no-JS verified for all three actions', and the grader stated plainly that no-JS was established by reading dialog.css and the emitted markup, not by a real browser run with scripting disabled; its stated above-a-9 clause (a sibling spec not broken) is that dimension's own failureExample, i.e. the bar rather than above it.

gradeResult.summary: All three destructive actions now sit behind per-subject confirmations built on one shared primitive, with collision-proof ids, the server write contract untouched, and a no-JS inline-card path that keeps every confirm button reachable in a single submit. Three dimensions land at 9 because their remaining passCriteria bullets - a page-wide duplicate-id scan, curl-level origin/conflict probes, and a real scripting-disabled browser run - were not performed.
